Yesterday, the US government announced an update to its list of banned foreign-made products, adding "advanced robotic devices." Today, a spokesperson for the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) confirmed that robotic vacuum cleaners also fall within the scope of the ban.

The robotic vacuum ban affects Roomba, Roborock, and other well-known brands—but you can still keep using the products you already own

The Trump administration announced yesterday a ban on "advanced robotic devices" entering the US, with headlines focusing on humanoid robots. Yet surveillance doesn't need legs, and the FCC's robot ban is no different. Katie Gorscak, the FCC's Director of Media Relations, confirmed to The Verge that robotic vacuum cleaners would also be included in this robot ban. The ban will not be retroactive to your existing Roomba, and companies may continue to import and sell approved models. But the government claims that future foreign robots will pose national security risks, and even robotic vacuum companies have suddenly been asked to commit to setting up factories in the US for production.

The FCC considers advanced robotic devices to carry national security risks, and the same applies to seemingly innocuous products such as robotic vacuum cleaners, robotic lawn mowers, and the like.

Unless a device is explicitly approved, or is manufactured domestically in the US, it cannot be sold in the US under any circumstances.

The top-liked comment was posted by CCATX

This really needs to stop! Routers, electric vehicles, and now even robotic vacuum cleaners are being banned? It's utterly absurd. I'm not naive—I never view China as anything other than an economic and political competitor—but this is just plain stupid. Generally speaking, the best technology—whether it's smartphones, EVs, or robotic vacuums—is made in China. We can only blame ourselves. Over the past four decades, we've made decision after decision to move production overseas, because we've never truly invested in domestic education, manufacturing, or infrastructure.

This has nothing to do with national security. Any sane person wouldn't think a robotic vacuum poses a real threat to the US. This is purely the Trump administration flaunting its authoritarian muscle and trying to circumvent further tariffs. If you want to bring manufacturing back to the US, you should put together a ten-year plan and actually start investing, because this isn't something that can be done overnight. But banning technology that people around the world use every day and that makes Americans' lives more convenient, while making life harder for US citizens, is absolutely not the right approach.

The impact of this ban on the robotic vacuum market is particularly severe, as top brands such as Roomba, Roborock, and Ecovacs are all Chinese-funded enterprises.

If you already own these products, you can still continue using them normally today—the FCC currently has no intention of seizing your robotic vacuum.

However, depending on how the ban develops, the robotic vacuum market could see dramatic upheaval in the short term. If all of this sounds familiar, it's because we saw a similar play out just months ago with the wireless router ban.

Will you continue using your existing robotic vacuum? What's your reason? Let us know in the comments.
